newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC HK bond index rose 0.27 pct to 123.28 in Feb.
newsitem.headline: HSBC HK bond index rose 0.27 pct to 123.28 in Feb.

text.p: HSBC Markets said its Hong Kong bond index rose to 123.28 in February 1997, a 0.27 percent increase over January 1997.
The sub-index for Hong Kong government paper increased by 0.29 percent, while the sub-index for non-Hong Kong government paper rose by 0.26 percent.

Compared with levels at end-February 1996, the overall index increased by 7.3 percent, the sub-index for Hong Kong government paper rose by 6.7 percent and the sub-index for non-Hong Kong government paper increased by 7.7 percent.
HSBC Markets said a strong U.S. dollar, benign U.S. economic data and investors' buying on dips caused U.S. Treasuries to rise in the first three weeks of February.
The 30-year Treasury bond yield hit a low of 6.5 percent during February, compared with 6.79 percent at the end of January, it said.

Treasuries slumped late in the month after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan warned in his congressional testimony of a possible tightening to fend off inflation, HSBC Markets said. The yield on the 30-year bond rose to 6.8 percent by the end of February.
The Hong Kong bond market tends to follow the U.S. Treasury market because Hong Kong's currency is pegged to the dollar.
Early in February, the local debt market was focused on worries over the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, HSBC Markets said.
But 10-year Exchange Fund Notes ended the month yielding 7.12 percent against 7.06 percent at the end of January, while short-dated rates stayed firm throughout February, it said.
